title: Lesson 9: Church Planting - Missions - Ministry Partners
description: Priscilla and Aquila had day jobs, an open home, and friends in God's mission. This lesson looks at who God puts beside you in His work, from your own church to the ends of the earth.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned how to disciple others, pouring into a few who will teach others also (2 Timothy 2:2). That is how the mission grows, one life at a time. Back in Lesson 1, you drew a personal ministry map from Acts 1:8. Now you will see who is on that map with you.

blocks.title: The Tentmakers
blocks.text:
Priscilla and Aquila were a married couple who made tents for a living. Forced out of Rome, they moved to Corinth, where they met a traveling church planter named Paul. "Because he was of the same trade he stayed with them and worked, for they were tentmakers by trade" (Acts 18:3). They worked side by side all week, and every Sabbath Paul reasoned about Jesus in the synagogue. God was already at work in Corinth, and a church was born.

Later the couple moved to Ephesus. When a gifted young preacher named Apollos came to town knowing only part of the story, they did not criticize him from a distance. They took him aside and "explained to him the way of God more accurately" (Acts 18:26), and Apollos went on to strengthen believers across Greece. Wherever they lived, a church met in their home.

Years later Paul called them "my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, who risked their necks for my life," and said all the churches of the Gentiles gave thanks for them (Romans 16:3-4). They never preached a famous sermon. They had a trade, an open door, and a willingness to work with others wherever God was moving.

This is how God has always spread His church: through ordinary people working together. Priscilla and Aquila did not have to choose between their day job and God's mission. Their workshop, their table, and their friendships all became part of it.
9.1 - What has God put in your hands that He could use in His mission?
Your Mission Map

Jesus sent His followers to be His witnesses "in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth" (Acts 1:8). For you, that mission moves out in four circles: your church, your city, new churches, and the nations. In every circle, there are four ways to take part: pray, give, serve, or go.
Your Church and Your City

Your local church is home base. It is where you are known, fed, corrected, and sent, and it is God's main plan for reaching the world. But one church cannot reach every corner of a city. That is where ministry partners come in. Campus ministries, pregnancy resource centers, food pantries, refugee ministries, and prison ministries gather believers to come alongside local churches and reach people a church might not reach on its own.
I thank my God in all my remembrance of you, always in every prayer of mine for all of you making my prayer with joy, because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now.

A good partner ministry loves Jesus, holds to the gospel, and sends you back to your church stronger, not away from it. It can be a great place to find your personal ministry, working shoulder to shoulder with others who love your city and the people in it who are far from God. Talk with your pastor before you jump in, and let your church family know where you serve so they can pray for you.
9.2 - Which people in your city break your heart, and who is already serving them?
Churches That Plant Churches
The church in Antioch did something costly. While they were worshiping, the Holy Spirit asked them to give away two of their best leaders.

While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." Then after fasting and praying they laid their hands on them and sent them off.

Much of the New Testament is the story of churches planting churches. New churches tend to reach people older churches do not, and they keep older churches from getting comfortable. Starting new congregations is one of the most effective ways the gospel spreads through a city.

You can be part of this without moving across town. You can pray for new churches and their planters by name. You can give to help a new church get started. You can serve on a launch team or at a new church's outreach. And some of you may hear God calling you to go with a team that starts a church in a neighborhood that needs one.
9.3 - Pray, give, serve, or go: which one is God stirring in you?
To the Nations
God's mission does not stop at the city limits. One day His throne will be surrounded by worshipers from every people on earth.

After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.

That scene is the goal. Missions is not the finish line. Worship is, and missions is needed wherever people do not yet worship Jesus. Thousands of people groups still have little or no access to the gospel. Many churches send missionaries together, so that a small congregation can have a part in reaching the far side of the world. You can pray for a people group by name, give generously, go on a short-term trip, and welcome the nations who already live near you, like refugee families and international students.
9.4 - Which people or place far from Jesus could you begin praying for by name?

This can feel like a lot. You are not the Savior of your city or the world. Jesus is, and He has already done the work that saves. You get to join Him, and you do not do it alone. Like Priscilla and Aquila, you take the next faithful step with the people God has put beside you.
Lesson 9 Review

Priscilla and Aquila used their trade, their home, and their friendships to help plant churches in three cities, and the churches gave thanks for them. God's mission moves out from your church to ministry partners in your city, to new churches, and to the nations. In every circle you can pray, give, serve, or go, and in every circle you go with others.
In the next lesson, you will put it all together, discover how God has shaped you to serve, and find your place on a team in your church.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
This lesson draws on "Why Plant Churches" by Tim Keller and Let the Nations Be Glad by John Piper.
